objections.claim_attacked: title/hypothesis: the 10000 DRC-error cap hides the MegaBoom congestion hotspot at the vertical line
objections.objection: The record only says the reporter suspected the cap, while the placement heatmap has a similar vertical line, so the MegaBoom vertical-line stop is ambiguous and the macro-overlap case alone does not prove that cap ordering caused that boundary.

mechanism_check: N-D — no chosen intervention was stated or shown implemented; the issue summary says it closed with 0 comments and no maintainer-described change, so there is no causal lever to evaluate.
evidence_check: ASSERT — post_state is only an issue closure, with no confirmation that random-sampling or most-interesting selection was implemented and no before/after DRC-report metric.
attribution_check: ABSENT — the record contains no direct_quote with participant/date/locator, and the thread summary explicitly says there were 0 comments, so there is no attributed statement supporting any intervention.
missing_from_story: The actual closed-as-completed reason and any linked commit/PR changing the 10000-error selection
Whether the cap is first-N deterministic, sorted by DRC type/location, or random after any change
Total DRC-error count versus the 10000 cap in the MegaBoom blob
Evidence separating the vertical-line stop from a true placement/congestion boundary
Whether the macro overlap was legal intended abutment or an illegal OBS/halo violation
Before/after GUI or report behavior showing whether macro-overlap errors become visible without deltaDebug.py
most_defensible_part: The concrete macro-overlap observation that the first 10000 errors omitted the macro-overlap errors until deltaDebug.py reduced the design, because it directly demonstrates how a fixed first-window cap can hide errors.
